newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST - Hydro 1996 pre-tax profits seen up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Hydro 1996 pre-tax profits seen up.

text.p: Norwegian industrial group Norsk Hydro ASA is expected to book 1996 pre-tax profits of 11.52 billion crowns, up from 11.09 billion in 1995, according to 10 analysts polled by Reuters.

Six of them said Hydro shares were a buy while three said they were a hold. The tenth analyst declined to give a recommendation. Of nine analysts polled before Hydro presented its nine-month results, seven said buy while two said hold.
Before the annual result, eight analysts giving a target price said the share should be worth around 415 crowns at year-end. The share closed at 372.50 crowns on Monday on the Oslo Bourse.
Trends in aluminium prices were of major interest to analysts as well as what some called Hydro's new strategy with greater focus on growth rather than on cost cuts.
"In the long term the Hydro share's development depends on how well the company succeeds with its growth strategy in the individual sectors," one said.
He predicted acquisitions of production capacity for fertilisers outside Europe and a light metals expansion outside of Norway -- both developments possibly taking place in Asia.
Most analysts believed Hydro would continue to increase its recoverable oil reserves through new finds and by using new technology.
In the short term Hydro's value was seen linked to commodity price swings.
Hydro will present the annual result on February 24:
NOTE -- *Estimated extraordinary writedowns of 400 million crowns on the Lille-Frigg field have been deducted from the oil and gas division's operating result.
